context_title: perrie you go your way meaning

entries.query: perrie you go your way meaning
entries.answer:
**You Go Your Way** is Perrie Edwards’ 2024 single about letting someone go without forcing a commitment, inspired by an early conversation with her fiancé Alex Oxlade-Chamberlain.[1][2]

## What the song is about
When they first started dating in 2016, Perrie was about to leave for a two-and-a-half-month Little Mix tour with Ariana Grande. She did not want to pressure him to wait, so she told him they could each follow their own path and see if they found each other again.[2][3]

Alex refused that idea and made the relationship official. Years later they were engaged and had their son Axel, which is why the lyric about laughing when they look back in five years lands as a happy ending in her telling.[4][2]

Perrie has summed it up as: if you love something, set it free. If it comes back, it is yours.[4]

## How the lyrics read
On the surface the song sounds like a breakup. The couple is driving home, there is already “a little space” between them, and the chorus keeps repeating “You go your way, I’ll go mine.”[5][6]

That tension is the point. Perrie has said the sound is upbeat and anthemic, but the theme sits in the moment *before* an ending: fear of saying goodbye, jokes covering pain, and the line “I’m not ok” under the “okay, okay, okay.”[6][7]

Fans have also heard it as leaving for university, ending a friendship, or any leap of faith where two people split and hope the timing works out later.[7]

## Why it can feel confusing
Perrie’s real story is not a breakup. It is her trying to release pressure, him choosing her anyway, and the relationship surviving. The lyrics still work as a parting song because they capture that scared, generous “don’t wait if you don’t want to” feeling, even when her own ending was the opposite.[2][7]
